remediation.issue: The bootstrap executes a remote installation script without inspection or version pinning.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the pipe-to-shell command with a pinned release download, checksum verification, local inspection, and a separate explicit execution step.

content.user_title: Build Playable Browser Games with Higgsfield
content.value_statement: Creating a coherent browser game requires coordinated design, assets, code, testing, and deployment. This skill guides that workflow through Higgsfield CLI and bundled asset tools.
actual_capabilities: Defines the core loop, controls, win conditions, performance budgets, and asset manifest before implementation.
Generates sprites, animation sheets, tileable textures, PBR maps, music, sound effects, voice, and 3D assets.
Builds solo, local multiplayer, and online multiplayer browser games using documented client and server contracts.
Converts, merges, inspects, rigs, and patches FBX or GLB assets with bundled Blender and Python scripts.
Tests games over local HTTP, packages source files, deploys updates, and publishes only after explicit user approval.
limitations: The workflow targets browser games, not native mobile, desktop, or console builds.
Updating an existing game requires its source files and existing game identifier.
Generation and deployment require Higgsfield CLI access, network connectivity, authentication, and available service credits.
Automated 3D rigging works best for humanoid T-pose characters; complex creatures may require procedural or manual correction.

use_cases.title: Create a Small Web Game
use_cases.description: Turn a concise concept into a tested solo browser game with coordinated visuals, audio, controls, and deployment.

use_cases.title: Prototype Multiplayer Rules
use_cases.description: Build a room-based game with server-authoritative state, reconnect behavior, hidden-information views, and two-session testing.

use_cases.title: Produce Game Assets
use_cases.description: Generate consistent sprites, textures, audio, or animated 3D models without deploying a complete game.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Beginner Game
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a simple solo browser game about [theme]. Include keyboard controls, one clear objective, a lose state, restart, sound effects, and deployment.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner has a small game idea and wants a playable result.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Cohesive Asset Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Create assets for a [genre] game in [visual style]. Produce [asset list], keep proportions consistent, and provide each asset with its manifest role.
prompt_templates.scenario: A designer needs production-ready visual or audio assets.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Online Multiplayer Game
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a two-player online [game type]. Use server-authoritative rules, private player views, reconnect support, responsive controls, and tests in two browser sessions.
prompt_templates.scenario: A developer needs a room-based multiplayer prototype.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Animated 3D Character
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a game-ready [character] from [reference]. Generate or transfer the rig, add [animation list], merge clips, inspect the GLB, and document quality limits.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs a verified animated character asset.

output: A transparent grid spritesheet with a consistent character silhouette.

output_examples.input: Build a private two-player card game with hidden hands.
output: A room-based playable URL with an invite flow and reconnect support.
Server-authoritative rules that reveal only each player's permitted state.

best_practices: Define the game profile, core loop, style formula, and asset manifest before generating assets or writing code.
Inspect model contracts before each generation type and preserve job records when chaining outputs.
Test the complete loop, responsive layout, assets, controls, restart behavior, and multiplayer sessions before deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not generate unrelated assets before establishing one consistent visual system.
Do not publish to a public marketplace without explicit user intent.
Do not deploy an update without the existing game identifier, because this creates a separate game.

faq.question: Can this skill build native mobile or desktop games?
faq.answer: No. It builds browser games, although responsive web games can support mobile browsers and touch controls.

faq.question: Can it create assets without building a full game?
faq.answer: Yes. It can produce sprites, textures, audio, or animated 3D assets and return their files or result URLs.

faq.question: Does it support multiplayer games?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports same-screen local multiplayer and room-based online multiplayer with platform server modules.

faq.question: What services are required?
faq.answer: Higgsfield CLI, an authenticated account, network access, and sufficient service credits are required for generation and deployment.

faq.question: Can it update an existing game?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the source files and existing game identifier so the workflow can preserve architecture and redeploy the same game.

faq.question: Will it publish my game automatically?
faq.answer: No. Deployment creates a playable URL, while public marketplace publication requires a separate request and explicit user approval.
